As the new school year begins, more and more Americans are expressing support for banning students from using their phones throughout the entire school day.

The new school year is underway, and support for banning iPhone use in classrooms continues to rise.

That's right, it's still July, but summer has ended without us noticing. My children will be returning to school today and tomorrow — this is the second consecutive year that the start of school no longer falls in August.

Apple is ushering in the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion, offering eligible students and educators a gift card of up to $150 with the purchase of select Mac and iPad products. The promotion runs through August 27. Consumers in several states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday offers.

Although back-to-school discounts are a pleasant surprise, the use of smartphones during class time is increasingly falling out of favour.

A recent Pew Research Center survey found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using their phones during class. This figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025, with only 18% now opposing classroom bans.

Support for stricter, full-day bans — from class time through to dismissal — has risen even more significantly. For the first time, a majority of Americans now support prohibiting students from using their phones throughout the entire school day.

The report also noted that younger generations remain less enthusiastic about both classroom and full-day bans, although support rates have risen across all age groups since 2024. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools restrict iPhone use only during class time, implement a full-day ban from class to dismissal, or leave the decision to students and parents? Let us know in the comments.
